summary.headline: Gandhar Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 92% YoY to INR 1,732 crore and PAT hit a record INR 206 crore on a per-kilolitre spread of INR 28,145.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue rose about 92% YoY to INR 1,732 crore and EBITDA reached INR 281 crore, with margin at 16.2% versus 5.1% a year earlier. PAT of INR 206 crore was the company's highest quarterly profit and exceeded the full FY26 profit, per management. Management attributed the spread expansion to exceptional Middle East-driven market conditions, sourcing from domestic base oil producers and higher realisations, and said it expects margins to stay near these levels for one to two quarters. Volume grew about 8% YoY to roughly 131,000 KL, and an interim dividend of 100% of face value was declared.

segments.name: PHPO (personal care, healthcare, pharma, performance oil)
segments.commentary: Primary growth engine with 18% YoY growth, driven by volume and wider revenue from existing customers. Management expects it to remain the star segment and indicated it stays above about 50% of total sales.

segments.name: PIO (process and insulating oil / transformer oil)
segments.commentary: Grew 28% YoY; management said PIO manufacturing volume rose from 14,000 KL to 18,000 KL. Demand from transformer, power and rubber customers; growth expected to be strong going forward.

segments.name: Lubricants
segments.commentary: Broadly stable, described as a resilient revenue base. Price increase taken in automotive lubricants with some delay due to the dealer-distributor network.

segments.name: Texol (Hamriyah Free Zone, Sharjah subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Operations temporarily hit by regional supply constraints and vessel disruptions in Q1; logistics gradually normalising. Management calls it strategically important and margin-accretive. Borrowings sit here, mostly working-capital plus some term loan.

guidance_outlook: Management is hopeful margins stay at or around current levels for most of FY27, and anticipates stellar levels for at least the next 1-2 quarters; said it is not reverting immediately.
Volume growth target of 8-10% (up to 11%) for FY27; management said revenue growth from value would also be higher.
Exports expected to hold at roughly the current share level; the company is aiming to increase export metrics over the year.
Capex plans to be announced in about the next quarter; company says internal accruals can fund capex without term loans, with term loans possible if needed.
Tax rate: 25% in India; blended consolidated rate of roughly 23-24% implied by management.
Interim dividend of 100% of face value declared; about INR 20 crore of Q1 profit earmarked for it.
capex_capacity: Installed capacity about 597,000 KL; all 3 plants together ran at about 97% on a two-shift basis, with third shift used when required.
Capacity is fungible across PHPO, PIO and lubricants; no segment-wise capacity split is disclosed.
Capex plans not yet announced; management is drawing them up and will update in about the next quarter.
Management said it has a debt-free standalone balance sheet and sufficient internal accruals for own-funded capex.
demand_pricing: Price increases were taken across PHPO, PIO and lubricants (automotive lubricants with a lag), per management.
Management attributed the spread to a mix of higher demand, higher realisations and agile raw material sourcing, and said sourcing was the bigger contributor in some answers.
Main base oil supply was from Saudi Arabia and South Korea; Hormuz disruption delayed Saudi shipments, so the company bought more from South Korea and domestic base oil producers at different prices.
Export realisations are about 5-6% higher than domestic realisations, per management.
Management estimates customer stocking of roughly 10-15% at most in the quarter, not a doubling.
Industry growth cited at 5%+ CAGR (CRISIL report) and 6-7% CAGR in a later answer; company has over 4,000 customers and exports to 100+ countries.
Channel partner volumes fluctuate and are not tracked to end industry; PIO is tender-based.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the margin expansion came from product mix versus inventory gains, and what is the full-year margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said inventory gains were minimal (raw material held 30-40 days); gains came mainly from higher selling prices. It is hopeful margins stay at or near current levels for most of the year.

qa_highlights.question: What are the volume and revenue growth expectations for FY27, and the export outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume growth of 8-10%, up to 11%, historically; value growth expected to be higher. Exports expected to remain at current levels, with an aim to grow export metrics.

qa_highlights.question: Is the spread sustainable, and what was the gross margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it expects margins at stellar levels for at least 1-2 quarters and will not revert immediately. Consolidated gross margin for the quarter was 21.4%. It declined to give forward guidance on the INR 28,000 spread.

qa_highlights.question: Why did PIO and channel partner volumes appear to decline YoY?
qa_highlights.answer: Channel partner volumes are lumpy and not tied to end industry. PIO manufacturing volume rose from 14,000 KL to 18,000 KL on a consolidated basis.

qa_highlights.question: What is the borrowing position and trade payables outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Standalone company is debt-free; borrowings are at Texol, mainly working capital plus declining term loan. Trade payables rose from INR 315 crore to INR 430 crore; about INR 600 crore of the INR 900-odd crore payables is not yet due and about 90% is within 90 days, with no rise in payable days.

qa_highlights.question: What are the tax rate and blended margin expectations for FY28-29?
qa_highlights.answer: India tax rate 25%; blended rate of roughly 23-24% implied. Management declined to give a sustainable margin run-rate beyond the current quarters.

risks_watch: Spread of INR 28,145/KL is far above the INR 8,274/KL normal level; management itself said it should be viewed in the context of exceptional conditions, and historical EBITDA margins were about 5-8%.
Supply risk from Hormuz disruption: Saudi shipments delayed, forcing costlier sourcing from South Korea and Indian producers.
Management repeatedly declined to guide on sustainable margin beyond 1-2 quarters or on the spread; watch Q2 FY27 spread and realisations.
Quality of growth: management said the top-line rise came from exports, realisations and new geographies; the export share jumped to 51% and exports were partly from 'certain opportunities on table'.
Receivables rose with revenue; watch working capital and Texol throughput as logistics normalise.
South Africa entry strategy not yet defined; revenue potential from Indonesia, Europe, USA and South Africa not quantified.
Customer concentration not disclosed; management said top-5 share is not significant across 4,000+ customers.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on the quarter, but cautious on forward numbers: management repeatedly called Q1 exceptional and avoided quantifying the spread, sustainable margin or segment capex beyond 1-2 quarters. Several answers were evasive or deferred, notably on the customer base, the South Africa plan and capex.
key_quotes: Quarter 1 '27 has been significant for Gandhar, delivering highest quarterly profit in the company's history.
While these spreads are significantly above historical levels, they should be viewed in the context of the exceptional market conditions witnessed during the quarter.
But obviously, we anticipate the margins would be continued to be at a stellar levels for at least the next 1 or 2 quarters to come.
So, the growth that we see in this industry of about 6% to 7% CAGR is more than enough for us to grow at about 8% to 10% in volume terms.

growth.why: FY27 volume growth guided at 8-10% (up to 11%), with Q1 volume up about 8% YoY to ~131,000 KL and utilisation ~97% on two shifts; no new capacity is announced and capex plans are due in about a quarter, so growth is only partly backed, while the 92% revenue jump is price and spread driven and management expects margins to hold near current levels for one to two quarters.
